prior_coverage:
Read first (free): research/measurements/crazygames.md (ticks 1-3; verdict NEEDS_MORE at :407-409); research/channel-loop/BOARD-LOOP.md candidate 6 (:122-127, CrazyGames), candidate 14 (:178-183, GameMonetize/GameDistribution/Playgama, 'only after a game has passed CrazyGames Basic Launch'), the Poki deferral (:192) and the Coolmath/Poki flat-licence deferral (:193); logs/CHANNEL_LOOP.md:120 (CrazyGames NEEDS_MORE) and :128 (syndication 'waiting'); research/channel-loop/scouts.json:184-231 (CrazyGames, networks, Poki, flat licences) and :301 note (3) (Microsoft Store dropped on its selfie step); research/colony-sweep/groups/storefronts.md:180 and scouts/storefronts--game-3d-assets.md:31-77 (itch.io judged only as an asset storefront, ceiling ₪0, AI policy unread); docs/REJECTED.md:1002 (itch.io in the licensing-ip audit). docs/REJECTED.md has no game-portal kill. Zero repo hits for Wavedash, Y8, Lagged, Newgrounds, Game Jolt, Kongregate, Armor Games or Famobi (grep 28.9). No game exists in products/.

Checked and dropped this sweep, so they are not rediscovered:
- Poki: the prior deferral stands; a 5-year exclusivity is confirmed first-hand in lucid-winds PUB-LISTINGS.md.
- Coolmath Games and Armor Games: each deal is a licence or sponsorship signed per game, the per-deal signature precedent at BOARD-LOOP.md:193.
- Famobi: affiliates need 50,000+ visits a month; developers are paid only after €250 accrues and they send an invoice carrying a tax ID, which is per-payout paperwork (plixfy evidence.md, github).
- Kongregate: closed to new web games since July 2020 (lucid-winds, github).
- Newgrounds: sources disagree on whether ad revenue share still exists; income may now come only from Monthly Portal Awards (lucid-winds, github).
- GamePix: non-payment complaints from Jan 2025; 30 games earned $0.12/day in total (plixfy evidence.md, github).
- Lagged: pays through the developer's own AdSense account, a new Google identity step. An Israeli developer's AdSense was rejected twice (ohadf2015/boggle-new, github).
- Yandex Games/Playhop: reachable through Playgama's partner list. Direct payouts are country-dependent from a Russian payer (UNKNOWN).
- Game Jolt: not researched, for lack of budget.

New evidence this sweep, all github grade unless stated:
- Playgama has an official Developer Cabinet MCP (Playgama/developer-cabinet-mcp). Submitting a game to moderation stays human-only.
- Wavedash has an official CLI for CI and cloud agents (wvdsh/cli, wvdsh/ai), but no store-page command.
- An Israeli developer's CrazyGames Basic Launch got 157K impressions and 209 plays and was rejected (ohadf2015/boggle-new).
- GameDistribution's terms, per a third-party reading: 33% share, NET 60, only EU-sanctions countries excluded. Payment-delay complaints run from 2018 to Jan 2025.
- itch.io requires a Generative AI disclosure (snippet).
- The butler CLI pushes builds from CI, but the HTML5 flag is set on the web edit page.

Cross-cutting: none of these rails (Tipalti, PayPal, Playgama bank/Wise, GameDistribution) has a ledger connector yet (scouts.json:188, :201). A PayPal connector would be needed before any of this money counts.

gate_zero_cost.evidence: No developer fee appears in the terms (crazygames.md T3.7, line 395). Hosting and CDN are CrazyGames' (faq.txt:646). The only named cost is multiplayer servers (faq.txt:664), so single-player games stay at ₪0.

gate_israel_payout_no_camera.evidence: The terms have no country clause (crazygames.md:363). Tipalti availability depends on country, with a 'Hold Payments' fallback (payouts.txt:293, 375-377). No camera, selfie or passport step is named on any captured page (crazygames.md:264-265). The payee is the owner's legal name (terms:547-549). Github: an Israeli developer got far enough to submit, which needs billing onboarding; that is not proof of payout.

gate_programmatic_listing.evidence: Upload is only through the portal, by drag and drop (faq.txt:650, 806). There is no API or CLI, and the terms are silent on automated submission (crazygames.md:376). Github: d954mas/game-67-idle .codex/skills/nt-portal-publish/SKILL.md fills CrazyGames drafts by browser automation but keeps the final 'submit' as a human's word. So automation is technically possible; whether it is permitted is unread, and the Publisher Guidelines (terms:63-66) are unread.

gate_ai_allowed_honest.evidence: The terms have no AI clause (crazygames.md:375). The FAQ's AI text is permissive advice, not a rule (faq.txt:786-796). The warranty 'original development by (employees of) Developer' (terms:396-397) is where an AI question would land. The binding Publisher Guidelines (terms:63-66) are unread.

gate_buyer_supply.evidence: faq.txt:679: 'over 50 million monthly active users'. faq.txt:503: in Basic Launch a game is 'shown to a small segment of players'. Github: the Israeli developer's game got 157K impressions in Basic Launch but only 209 plays at 0.2% CTR.

candidates.discovery_needs_prior_sale: No. Every accepted game gets an allocated player segment by rule (faq.txt:503), and promotion to Full Launch turns on Basic Launch metrics (terms:46-48), not on earlier sales. But impressions are not plays: 157K impressions produced 209 plays at 0.2% CTR (github), so the thumbnail and the first minute decide whether the audience turns into play.
candidates.owner_step:

- Proposed step 8: a brand mailbox, for acceptance emails (faq.txt:573) and the duty to 'promptly respond' (terms:209-210).
- Step 2 (the tax file).

Per game: one portal upload. It is owner-free only if the board rules that a runner-driven brand login is acceptable; that ruling is still open.
candidates.estimate_basis:
INFERENCE, not a measured rate.
- Basic Launch pays ₪0 by contract (terms:238-240; faq.txt:420).
- The Full Launch rate is a formula with no number (crazygames.md T3.1).
- The one Israeli comparable failed Basic Launch (github).
- High case: 2-3 of about 10 agent-built games reach Full Launch and each earns roughly €50-60 a month. Top strategy games average 21 ad impressions per play (SimNyborg/ageborn docs/research/market-portals.md, github).
- The €100 threshold and payment 30 days after the self-bill (terms:284-298) push the first ledger row late, and no Tipalti or PayPal connector exists (scouts.json:188).
candidates.time_to_first_sale: At least 3-5 months after step 10, and only if a game passes. That is 5-10 agent-days to build, 7-21 days of Basic Launch, Full Launch QA, a month's accrual toward €100, the invoice early the next month, and payment 30 days after it.

candidates.existing_product: None. No game exists yet; it would reuse the CrazyGames build at about 1 agent-day per network (scouts.json:207).
candidates.listings_per_owner_step: One developer account plus one PayPal account puts every game into a public JSON/RSS feed that partner sites import. A third party pulled 5,001 games from rss.gamemonetize.com/rssfeed.php (RUDY4K/plixfy research_report.md), against a marketed '36,976+'.
candidates.prior_verdict: Queue rank 14: 'only after a game has passed CrazyGames Basic Launch' (BOARD-LOOP.md:178-183). logs/CHANNEL_LOOP.md:128 says 'waiting'. scouts.json:197-207 notes the USDT leg is dead and the RPM claims are SEO copy. Not rejected.
candidates.reopen_basis: Not rejected. New: the GameMonetize FAQ snippet gives 'more than 45%' share, NET30 ('within 25 days'), a $30 PayPal minimum, 'PayPal and USDT ERC20 to all countries', and external links and branding allowed. The board's sequencing rule (after CrazyGames Basic Launch) stands.

gate_zero_cost.evidence: The FAQ names a revenue share and a payout minimum and no developer fee (gamemonetize.com/faq snippet); the share is taken out of ad revenue. Absence of a fee is not stated as policy.

gate_israel_payout_no_camera.evidence: 'PayPal and USDT ERC20 to all countries' (FAQ snippet; github plixfy research_report.md). USDT is dead on the crypto off-ramp kill (scouts.json:204). PayPal is a new owner account. An Israeli PayPal account withdraws to an Israeli bank in ILS (snippet, research/colony-sweep/scouts/payment-rails--paypal-israel.md:24). Whether GameMonetize or PayPal onboarding needs a camera step is UNKNOWN.

gate_programmatic_listing.evidence: Submission is by web dashboard or email ('info@gamemonetize.com + gamemonetize.com/joinus', lucid-winds marketing/OUTREACH_CONTACTS.md row 5). GitHub code search found no developer upload API. The public feed serves publishers, not submissions. The terms on automated access are unread.

gate_ai_allowed_honest.evidence: No AI rule found: the web search returned none and the terms are unread.

gate_buyer_supply.evidence: A third party confirmed the public feed with a 'Newest' sort is live (plixfy research_report.md; scouts.json:205). The 45%+45% developer/publisher split exists because third-party sites embed the games. Numbers are inflated: 5,001 in the feed against 36,976 claimed. Credit-risk signal: default probability 0.709 (Nov 2024, per plixfy evidence.md).

candidates.discovery_needs_prior_sale: Partly no. Partner sites that auto-import the feed's 'Newest' sort surface a new game with no history (scouts.json:205, github). Placement under the other sorts and on partner sites is UNKNOWN.
candidates.owner_step: One-time: a GameMonetize developer account under the brand (new, proposed), a PayPal account in the owner's legal name (new, not in steps 1-7), the brand mailbox (proposed step 8), and step 2. Per game: a dashboard upload, unless the board admits a runner-driven login.
candidates.estimate_basis: INFERENCE. The only per-game yield in reach comes from a comparable network: GamePix paid about $0.12/day for 30 games and about $0.1/day for 20 (plixfy evidence.md, github). GameMonetize's own $1.5-3 RPM is SEO copy (scouts.json:205). Share is 45%, threshold $30. High case: 15-20 games that each keep a small feed placement.
candidates.time_to_first_sale: 3-12 months after the owner steps. Review time is UNKNOWN; at GamePix-like yields, reaching $30 takes months, and payment then follows NET30.

candidates.reopen_basis: New github evidence: Playgama/developer-cabinet-mcp (created 11.9.2026, v1.1.0), an official OAuth MCP at developer.playgama.com/api/mcp. It lets an agent create a game draft, upload the build and covers, fill the form, and run a public sandbox with free DSP traffic. But: 'These stay human actions in the cabinet: submitting a game to moderation; ... reading payouts; uploading screenshots, videos and other assets.' Snippet: payouts need account verification by email naming a director or authorised signatory. Developer share is 70/80/90% on partner sites, 50% on playgama.com and 75% on YouTube Playables (wiki.playgama.com payments FAQ).

gate_zero_cost.evidence: No fee appears in any reading: d954mas playgama.md found no fee passages, and plixfy likewise. Revenue shares only.

gate_israel_payout_no_camera.evidence: 'payments to a bank account in any country' plus crypto on request (wiki.playgama.com, quoted in plixfy research_report.md, github); PayPal and Wise are listed as well (elite-3d-design-studio 01-portal-buyers.md, github). Payout verification is by email with a director's or signatory's name, and further documents 'may be requested' (snippet). A camera step, and whether an individual rather than a company is accepted, are UNKNOWN.

gate_programmatic_listing.evidence: The official MCP automates create, upload, covers and form. But submission to moderation is explicitly a human action in the cabinet (developer-cabinet-mcp README), and every new archive must pass moderation again (playgama.md S10). That is one human click per game and per update, the recurring per-item owner action the mandate forbids (BOARD-LOOP.md:9 item (g)). Moderation of the first game also 'opens a chat in your preferred messenger' (playgama.md S1). Reopens if Playgama adds submission to the MCP (it is 2 weeks old), or if the owner says yes to one click per game.

gate_ai_allowed_honest.evidence: 'AI-generated assets are allowed', but 'Platforms will reject low-quality titles constructed wholly with generative AI that bring nothing fresh'. AI-graphics titles perform 'more than 2x worse on metrics'; story, logic and maths via AI are fine (playgama.md S7). Playgama itself publishes Claude Code plugins (Playgama/bridge-claude-plugins).

gate_buyer_supply.evidence: 24 partner platforms (playgama.md S9). Sandbox DSP traffic: 'free traffic is a share bonus and takes 1–3 public post links' (MCP README). Catalogue page title '18078 games' (scouts.json:206). No player counts.

candidates.discovery_needs_prior_sale: No at entry. After moderation the game goes out to the partner platforms, and a sandbox build can receive free DSP traffic. Ranking inside each partner platform after that is performance-based (UNKNOWN).
candidates.owner_step: One-time: a Playgama developer account (new, proposed), OAuth consent for the MCP, the payout-verification email from the registered address, a payout method (bank, PayPal or Wise), the brand mailbox (step 8), and step 2. Recurring, and the reason for the FAIL: one 'submit to moderation' click per game and per update, plus a messenger chat with moderation for the first game.
candidates.estimate_basis: INFERENCE. Shares of 50-90% (snippet), but per-platform volumes are unknown. AI-graphics titles do 2x worse (github). The GamePix per-game yield serves as the floor analogue. Breadth multiplies a small per-platform number. $100 withdrawal threshold.
candidates.time_to_first_sale: 2-6 months after the owner steps: moderation takes 1-5 business days and partner portals up to 2 weeks (playgama.md S2, S10), then the $100 threshold and payout verification.

gate_zero_cost.evidence: 'Wavedash charges 10% ... developers keep the rest' (wavedash.com/developers, snippet). No fee found.

gate_israel_payout_no_camera.evidence: The payout rail, countries and KYC were not found. Wavedash is a US YC startup; that it pays through Stripe is INFERENCE, and Stripe does not onboard Israeli accounts.

gate_programmatic_listing.evidence: The official CLI takes a token for 'CI, cloud agents, or headless environments' (wvdsh/ai skills/wavedash/references/cli.md), and project create, build push and publish --yes are all scriptable. gate_ai_allowed_honest.evidence: The content rules ban crypto/NFT, gambling, hate, impersonation and browser-crashing; there is no AI ban (publishing.md). Wavedash ships official Claude, Codex and Cursor plugins (wvdsh/ai). No disclosure rule found; the content-guidelines page is unread.

gate_buyer_supply.evidence: A young platform (a $4.3M raise, per a GamesBeat snippet); no player numbers were found.

candidates.owner_step: One-time: a Wavedash account and team (new, proposed), WAVEDASH_TOKEN as a repository secret, payout onboarding (rail unknown), the brand mailbox, and step 2.
candidates.estimate_basis: INFERENCE. A 90% share of paid-content sales (snippet), but the audience is unknown, and every sale needs a player who chooses to pay after playing free.
candidates.time_to_first_sale: Weeks after publishing, if the platform has players. Payout timing is unknown.
